---
title: "Random Survival Forest Variable Screening"
author:
  - "**[Editor]** ZCode (GLM) — AI-generated, independently AI-reviewed;"
---

A random survival forest (**RSF**) ranks variables by how much out-of-bag (OOB) permutation degrades prediction, giving a screening path for survival omics: univariate-Cox pre-filter → RSF → relative importance → signature cutoff \[1\]. The two reference panels answer different questions — (A) the OOB error rate vs number of trees (has the forest converged?) and (B) relative importance (which variables carry predictive weight?) — and the reference's original engine `randomSurvivalForest::rsf()` is CRAN-archived, so this tutorial uses its maintained successor `randomForestSRC::rfsrc()`, whose objects carry the same `$err.rate` and `$importance` slots:

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(survival)
})
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

200 simulated patients × 40 genes with six planted prognostic genes (coefficients aligned to the planted positions, weak enough that the OOB error declines visibly over hundreds of trees). The reference pipeline pre-filters by univariate Cox p < 0.05 before the forest — the same step here, so the RSF sees only pre-screened variables:

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(survival)})
if (!requireNamespace("randomForestSRC", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("randomForestSRC", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
set.seed(18201)
## 200 patients x 40 genes; 6 genes planted as prognostic
n <- 200; n_gene <- 40
genes <- sprintf("GENE%02d", 1:n_gene)
expr <- matrix(rnorm(n * n_gene, 4, 1.2), n, n_gene, dimnames = list(NULL, genes))
prognostic <- c("GENE03", "GENE11", "GENE19", "GENE24", "GENE31", "GENE38")
coef <- c(0.32, -0.28, 0.34, 0.28, -0.32, 0.38)
## align coefficients with the PLANTED positions (a positional c(coef, 0, 0, ...)
## here silently makes columns 1-6 the prognostic genes instead)
full_coef <- rep(0, n_gene); full_coef[match(prognostic, genes)] <- coef
lp <- as.vector(scale(as.vector(expr %*% full_coef)))
lam <- exp(lp)
OS.time <- pmin(3000, pmax(30, qweibull(runif(n), 1, 1200 / lam)))
OS <- rbinom(n, 1, pmin(0.9, pmax(0.05, 0.5 + 0.25 * lp)))
dt.rf <- data.frame(OS.time = OS.time, OS = OS, expr)
## univariate Cox pre-filter (p < 0.05), as in the reference pipeline
cox_p <- vapply(genes, function(g)
  summary(coxph(Surv(OS.time, OS) ~ get(g), data = dt.rf))$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"], numeric(1))
gene.sel <- names(cox_p)[cox_p < 0.05]
```

## Visualization

### 1. Error-Rate Curve and Importance Lollipop

The two reference panels: the OOB error rate falls and plateaus as trees accumulate (Panel A — this is how `ntree` is chosen), and the rescaled importance lollipop ranks genes relative to the top one with the 0.2 cutoff dashed (Panel B — the six planted genes top the ranking, with two weak noise genes just over the line, which is exactly what a real screen looks like):

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1RfSurv
#| fig-cap: "Random survival forest screening of 200 simulated patients: OOB error rate vs number of trees (left) and relative importance of Cox-prefiltered genes rescaled to the top gene with a 0.2 cutoff (right); the six planted prognostic genes top the ranking."
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(randomForestSRC))
## randomForestSRC::rfsrc() replaces the archived randomSurvivalForest::rsf()
surv.rf <- rfsrc(Surv(OS.time, OS) ~ ., data = dt.rf[, c("OS.time", "OS", gene.sel)],
                 ntree = 500, importance = TRUE, seed = 12345678)
## Panel A: OOB error rate vs number of trees (rfsrc records the trace
## only every 10th tree — plot the recorded positions)
err.rate <- as.vector(surv.rf$err.rate)
err.idx <- which(!is.na(err.rate))
## Panel B: relative importance (rescaled to the top gene) lollipop
raw.imp <- surv.rf$importance
rel.imp <- raw.imp / max(abs(raw.imp))
imp.cutoff <- 0.2
sel <- sort(rel.imp[rel.imp > imp.cutoff])

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
par(bty = "o", mgp = c(1.5, .33, 0), mar = c(3.5, 4, 2.5, 1), las = 1, tcl = -0.25)
plot(err.idx, err.rate[err.idx], type = "l", lwd = 1.5,
     xlab = "Number of Trees", ylab = "", main = "OOB error rate")
mtext("Error Rate", side = 2, line = 2.2, las = 3)
par(bty = "o", mgp = c(1.5, .33, 0), mar = c(3.5, 6, 2.5, 1), las = 1, tcl = -0.25)
xrange <- range(pretty(range(sel)))
plot(NA, NA, xlim = xrange, ylim = c(0.5, length(sel) + 0.5),
     xlab = "Variable Relative Importance", ylab = "", yaxt = "n",
     main = "OOB relative importance")
abline(v = imp.cutoff, lty = 2, col = "grey55")
for (i in seq_along(sel)) lines(c(xrange[1], sel[i]), c(i, i), col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5)
axis(2, at = seq_along(sel), labels = gsub("_", "-", names(sel)), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   `rfsrc()` records the per-tree error trace **only every 10th tree** (`err.rate` has `NA` between) — plot the non-`NA` positions or the line silently disappears.
-   Align simulation (or real) coefficients with the right variable **positions**: a positional `c(coef, 0, 0, ...)` aligned to columns 1-6 while the intended genes sit elsewhere produces a figure that is internally consistent but biologically wrong.
-   The relative importance is rescaled to `max(abs(importance))`, so the cutoff (0.2 here; the reference's paper used 0.65) is a **relative** threshold — report it together with the raw importances and treat it as a ranking device, not evidence.
:::

## Applications

::: {#fig-RfSurvApplications1}
![](../images/RfSurvivalPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="RSF variable screening" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

RSF variable screening
:::

The same two-panel readout serves any censored-outcome forest: clinical-only risk models, radiomics feature screening, or CNV-gene signature selection before multivariate modelling.
